spec.assertion: Structural: every burstCdr-carrying block has trigger.kind 'fullBurstEnter' and target {allies, !excludeSelf}. Fails under the burstCast re-key (the over-crediting nearest-wrong) and under a self-scoped target. Structural rather than behavioural because liter is the B1 in this fixture, so burstCast and fullBurstEnter fire the same number of times ~1.5s apart and are behaviourally degenerate.

Every authored burstCdr.seconds is drawn from the kit ladder {2.34, 2.7, 3.17} or its running totals {5.04, 8.21} and at least one reaches >=3.17; oncePerBattle is never set. Fails under a fudged/rounded magnitude, under a flat-2.34-forever model (never reaches 3.17), and under a once-per-battle encoding.

spec.kitLine: CDR is real + reaches all allies
spec.assertion: Behavioural: stripping all burstCdr effects strictly reduces the fullBurstStart count; retargeting them to self strictly reduces it too (liter's own 20s cooldown is not the chain gate, the Burst III carry's is). Fails if the CDR is absent, inert, or self-scoped. NOTE this is the highest-risk assertion in the file: it presumes the rotation is cooldown-bound rather than gauge-bound in the 4-unit control comp. If it goes RED with a faithful override, the finding is that liter's headline mechanic is inert in this fixture, which is itself worth surfacing.
it.skip - burstCdr emits no event, so the per-entry magnitude cannot be separated from the gauge/chain constraints. Only presence, magnitude set, scope and direction are testable.

Structural: every block carrying the 45.17 / 12.46 / 14.42 buffs has trigger.kind 'burstCast' and target {allies, !excludeSelf}. Fails under the fullBurstEnter re-key, which over-credits whenever another unit completes the chain.

Event count == literCasts * teamSize with teamSize distinct targets including liter herself, stat maxAmmoPct. Fails under replace-semantics (tier 1 would stop after cast 1), under excludeSelf, and under a maxAmmoFlat encoding (45.17 is a percentage, not rounds).

Event count == ammoCount - teamSize, i.e. exactly one cast fewer than tier 1, and >0. This is the accumulate-vs-replace shape as arithmetic: fails under no-tiering (counts would be equal), under replace-semantics (crit would fire on cast 2 only = teamSize events), and under an off-by-one tier gate.

Event count == ammoCount - 2*teamSize and >0 (non-vacuity: the fixture reaches >=3 casts); value emitted as the raw 14.42 with zero casterAtkPct events from liter (rules out the caster-scaled flat-resolve mis-encoding); zeroing it strictly lowers the carry's damage (rules out authored-but-inert).
durationShots undefined and expiresFrame finite on every tier event. Fails under a ROUND-count encoding and under a permanent encoding.

Removing every skill2 block leaves ALL units' totals byte-identical. This is the tandem-trap probe: the control comp contains an on-recovery consumer, so if the cover restore were modelled as a `heal` effect it would fire that consumer every cycle and this goes RED. My blind reading is that cover HP is a separate resource from unit HP and does NOT constitute a recovery, so the line must be offensively inert. FLAG: this is the one adjudication point in the file - if cover restoration is ruled to fire recovery triggers, this assertion is the divergence, not the bug.
it.skip - no cover-HP pool in v1 and no target kind for 'lowest remaining COVER HP'; payload unobservable.

it.skip + FLAG - the prose gives no trigger, so cadence falls to the interval-at-datamined-skill-cooldown convention, and that cooldown is NOT in this packet (the 20s quoted is the burst cooldown). Damage-inert either way under my reading.

One buffApply per ally per cast (count == ammoCount, cross-checking that both ride the same cast), stat atkPct, value exactly 66 with a finite expiresFrame and no durationShots. Fails under casterAtkPct/highestAllyAtkPct (which re-emit as a flat ATK number in the thousands), under excludeSelf, and under a round-count duration.

Zeroing the 66% strictly lowers BOTH the carry's and liter's own totals; retargeting to self strictly lowers the carry's total while leaving liter's byte-identical. The paired equality is what makes the target set unambiguous - a mis-scoped buff cannot satisfy both halves. All three patches are damage-only (shot counts and rotation untouched), so the strict inequalities are safe.
Deleting durationSec strictly raises the carry's damage. Fails (no delta) if the window was already encoded as permanent - the direct discriminator for the duration-semantics trap.

fixtures: controlComp('rapi-red-hood', true) for all 8 runs. liter occupies controlComp's Burst I slot by construction, so the carry argument MUST be a different unit - controlComp('liter') would duplicate her. A Burst III carry is required for the chain to complete at all (a lone B3 makes zero Full Bursts) and a long-cooldown B3 is what lets liter's burst-CD reduction bind; helm=true keeps the 4-unit team so the gauge fills fast and the COOLDOWN, not the gauge, gates the rotation - a gauge-bound fixture cannot discriminate a CDR claim. Deterministic, no seed. Six of the seven counterfactuals are damage-only patches (strict damage inequalities are therefore safe); the two CDR patches are expected to move the rotation and are judged on fullBurstStart counts instead. Run budget: 8 full 180s sims.
gaps: skill1 s1-A exact cumulative CDR ladder (2.34 / 5.04 / 8.21 by entry index) - burstCdr emits no event; only the downstream rotation effect is visible and it cannot be separated from the gauge/chain constraints. Magnitude SET and accumulate-vs-replace shape are covered structurally instead.
skill2 cover-HP restore amount (52.5%) and the '2 lowest remaining cover HP' target set - no cover-HP pool and no matching target kind in v1; payload unobservable.

skill2 firing cadence - FLAG: the prose carries no activation clause, so the trigger falls to the interval-at-datamined-skill-cooldown convention and that cooldown is not in this packet. Damage-inert under my reading either way.

skill1 tier-1 Max Ammunition 45.17% DAMAGE impact - deliberately NOT asserted. A 5s ammo-capacity window may be genuinely behaviour-neutral if the engine only reads maxAmmo at reload, so a strict damage-differential assertion risks a false RED against a faithful override. The line is fully covered on the event side (stat / value / tier / scope / target).
